context.title: Different kinds of document
context.text: A declaration justifies an action; a constitution allocates powers; an amendment changes rules. Their sentences do different political work.

context.title: Promise and exclusion
context.text: Universal language coexists with institutions that exclude or subordinate people. Later changes respond to conflicts the original arrangements did not resolve.
context.takeaway: Compare who is named with who is protected.

notice.why: The collection records revision, not a single timeless statement.

opening: Declaring independence is one task; building a government strong enough to survive and restrained enough to trust is another. These documents move from the claim that people may replace oppressive rulers to the detailed allocation of powers, rights, and prohibitions. Their promises coexist with exclusions that later amendments confront. Read together, they show a republic being declared, constructed, and revised, with arguments over who counts among its people written into the words that generations would use to demand a place within it.
